title: Your embarkation city is not an airport.
subtitle: Two nights before the ship is the cheapest upgrade in cruising.

text: Most people see Athens, Venice or Lisbon through a taxi window.
sub: The itinerary calls it day one and a transfer. It is a city with a season, a table worth booking, and a morning you do not get back.

title: Four reasons to come in ahead

items.head: A flight delay stops being a crisis
items.body: The missed-embarkation stories that end worst are flight stories, not late-tour stories. A spare night solves it.

items.head: You board rested
items.body: Day one is the most wasted day of any voyage when it follows an overnight flight and a queue.

items.head: The city, properly
items.body: Two nights ashore is a short holiday attached to a voyage, for the price of a hotel room.

items.head: Your luggage arrives with you
items.body: A bag that misses a connection can still reach a hotel. It cannot reach a ship that has sailed.

points.label: Land 11:00, sail 17:00
points.value: Terminal queue, muster, unpacking, sleep. The city never happened at all.

points.label: Arrive two days early
points.value: An afternoon, a dinner, a full night's sleep and a morning market.

points.label: Boarding at 13:00
points.value: Aboard ahead of the crowd, lunch at a quiet table on a half-empty ship.

points.label: Sail-away
points.value: On deck watching a place you know, rather than one you flew over.

quote: The night before a voyage isn't travel time. It's the first night of the holiday, and it's the one people cut.

title: Save this before you book the flights.
body: Air and hotel are part of the itinerary, not an afterthought to it. Tell me your embarkation city and I'll tell you how many nights it deserves.
